overview: Pacific systems keep the Northwest and Cascades wet through the weekend, with rain low and snow only up high. The northern Rockies and central Rockies get a stronger push of snow Friday into Saturday, while the Sierra and British Columbia stay mostly unsettled.

regions.title: Cascades
regions.text: A series of Pacific disturbances keeps the Cascades busy. Rain falls on the lower slopes and snow stays up high, with strong winds Thursday. Crystal Mountain has the best total in the region at 37". Snow comes back in heavier waves Friday and again Sunday.

regions.title: Northern Rockies
regions.text: A system moves into western Wyoming Friday and brings snow through Saturday. Snow is also possible east of the Continental Divide Saturday, though forecasters say the band's exact position is still uncertain. Grand Targhee leads the region with a peak of 24 inches Saturday.

regions.title: Coast Mountains
regions.text: Whistler and Cypress see rain and mixed showers through much of the week, with snow mostly restricted to the upper mountain. Whistler's biggest day is Wednesday, with 12 inches. Cypress picks up its best snow Sunday, when a stronger system pushes in.

regions.title: Tahoe
regions.text: A weakening front brings rain to the Sierra before drying out Wednesday. The next real snow arrives Sunday, when rain turns to snow. Palisades and Sugar Bowl each have 18 inches forecast for Sunday.

regions.title: Kootenays
regions.text: Mild, wet weather dominates the Kootenays this week. Snow levels run high, so most precipitation falls as rain at lower elevations. Whitewater's best day is Thursday, with 11 inches, and flurries return Sunday.

regions.title: Central Rockies
regions.text: Thanksgiving stays mild and dry across Colorado. A system arrives Friday night and runs into Saturday, but forecasters disagree on how strong it will be. Steamboat leads with a peak of 12 inches Saturday, and Vail sees 8 inches that day. Higher totals are possible if the stronger scenario wins out.

regions.title: Okanagan
regions.text: Showers are the main story in the Okanagan, with the heaviest rain Wednesday and Thursday. Snow stays mostly up high. Big White's best day is Thursday, with 8 inches.

regions.title: Northeast
regions.text: Le Massif is forecast for about 9". Mont-Sainte-Anne and Tremblant follow. Special Weather Statement at Le Massif from Friday to Saturday.

sources.name: NOAA buoys 51001 / 51101 (method: Powder Buoy, Mike Ruzek)

buoy.text: Buoys 51001 and 51101 near Hawaii popped Nov 11, the swell signal Powder Buoy watches for a Wasatch storm about two weeks later — here Nov 22–28. In past winters a pop raised the chance of a Wasatch storm in that window by roughly 6 to 12 points. Experimental: promising, not proven.
